main:1.text: In the Beginning is the introductory mission of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which introduces the protagonist Carl Johnson and shows his return to his home in Grove Street in the neighborhood of Ganton, Los Santos.

main:2.text: Big Smoke is the second storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which protagonist Carl Johnson performs independently at the Johnson House in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. There is no gameplay during this mission, as it is simply formed by two cutscenes.

main:3.text: Sweet & Kendl is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which protagonist Carl Johnson performs automatically after returning to his house in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl and Big Smoke arrive at the cemetery in Vinewood. They are greeted by Carl's sister Kendl, while fellow gang member Ryder looks on.

main:4.text: Ryder is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Lance "Ryder" Wilson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl drops by Ryder's house in Grove Street. Ryder does not seem that excited to see Carl back.

main:5.text: Tagging Up Turf is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl arrives at Sweet's house, where Sweet and Big Smoke are playing basketball. Sweet questions if Carl is really back for good. Sweet hands Carl a can of spray paint and tells him to go spray over enemy tags.

main:6.text: Cleaning the Hood  is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. The mission introduces the drugs aspect of the storyline, explaining how it has corrupted Los Santos.

main:7.text: Drive-Thru is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl arrives at Sweet's house to find Sweet, Smoke, and Ryder walking out. Smoke suggests getting something to eat. Carl, Sweet, Smoke and Ryder get into Sweet's car and drive to Cluckin' Bell in Willowfield.

main:8.text: Nines and AK's  is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl arrives at Sweet's house, where Sweet, Smoke and Ryder are playing dominoes. Carl asks what type of guns Grove Street Families have at the moment.

main:9.text: Drive-By is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl arrives at Sweet's doorstep where he overhears Ryder talking to Sweet, criticising Carl's driving skills, with Ryder oblivious to the fact Carl is standing behind him.

main:10.text: Sweet's Girl is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl Johnson drops by his brother's house. Upon arrival, however, he realises that nobody is home. Carl walks out of the house and receives a phone call from Sweet.

main:11.text: Cesar Vialpando is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl drops by Sweet's house, only to find Sweet and Kendl arguing over the latter's relationship with Cesar Vialpando, the leader of the Varrios Los Aztecas.

main:13.text: Running Dog is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Melvin "Big Smoke" Harris from his home in Idlewood, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl goes to Smoke's house. Upon arriving there, he finds Dr. Officer Frank Tenpenny and Officer Eddie Pulaski leaving. Smoke informs Carl that they are attempting to extract information from him.

main:14.text: Wrong Side of the Tracks is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Melvin "Big Smoke" Harris from his home in Idlewood, Los Santos, San Andreas. Dr. Tenpenny and Pulaski are seen leaving Big Smoke's house from the garage. Carl arrives and Smoke tells him that they have to go to the train station at Unity Station.

main:15.text: Just Business is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Melvin "Big Smoke" Harris from his home in Idlewood, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl drops by Big Smoke's house and finds him in the garage. They agree to take a ride somewhere, as Smoke has business to take care of. They head to Commerce and Big Smoke enters the Atrium.

main:16.text: Home Invasion is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Lance "Ryder" Wilson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. This mission can only be triggered between 12:00 and 20:00. Carl goes to see Ryder at his house. Carl walks into Ryder's backyard where he sees Ryder digging holes all across the lawn.

main:17.text: Catalyst is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Lance "Ryder" Wilson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl pays another visit to Ryder, who is making his own "water" (marijuana dipped in embalming fluid and then laced with PCP) after he couldn't find the stash he buried in his back yard. While Carl and Ryder are talking, Dr.

main:18.text: Robbing Uncle Sam is the final mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Lance "Ryder" Wilson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl goes to see Ryder in his back yard, who is smoking. He asks Carl why he, himself, didn't finish high school.

main:19.text: High Stakes, Low-Rider is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando from his home in El Corona, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl attains a lowrider car and drops by Cesar's house in El Corona. The two drive to the street race's starting point near the Commerce district and race against four other cars.

main:20.text: Life's a Beach is an Open Wheel Race featured in Grand Theft Auto Online as part of the Los Santos Summer Special update, released on August 11, 2020. It is available for up to 16 players. The race is a 36 checkpoint long Lap race, default to 10 laps. The pit lane is located between checkpoints 34 and 1. It takes place above the sea near Chumash. The racers start on the pit straight facing south-east.

main:21.text: Madd Dogg's Rhymes is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families affiliate and aspiring rapper Jeffrey "OG Loc" Cross from the Burger Shot he works at in the Marina, Los Santos, San Andreas. The mission introduces the player to the ability of stealth kills.

main:22.text: Management Issues is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families affiliate and aspiring rapper Jeffrey "OG Loc" Cross from the Burger Shot he works at in the Marina, Los Santos, San Andreas. Now, OG Loc has the technology and the ghostwritten lyrics to kickstart his rap career, but it seems he isn't fully satisfied yet.

main:23.text: House Party is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families affiliate and aspiring rapper Jeffrey "OG Loc" Cross from his house in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. The first part of the mission starts at Burger Shot in Marina, and then the actual mission starts afterward. The mission can only be accessed between 20:00 and 6:00.

main:24.text: Burning Desire is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by C.R.A.S.H. officers Frank Tenpenny, Eddie Pulaski and Jimmy Hernandez from the Jim's Sticky Ring doughnut shop in Market, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl enters the doughnut shop and is spotted by Frank Tenpenny, who tells him to come and sit with them.

main:25.text: Gray Imports is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by C.R.A.S.H. officers Dr. Frank Tenpenny, Eddie Pulaski and Jimmy Hernandez from the Jim's Sticky Ring doughnut shop in Market, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl goes to the Ocean Docks Freight Depot, where the Ballas and Russians are having a deal.

main:26.text: Doberman is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from the Ammu-Nation store in Market, Los Santos, San Andreas. The mission serves as a tutorial for gang warfare and the assets income.

main:27.text: Los Sepulcros is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. This mission can only be triggered between 9:00 and 17:00. The Ballas are holding a funeral for Little Weasel (who Carl and Big Smoke killed), and, according to Sweet, all of the Ballas OG's are going to be there.

main:28.text: Reuniting the Families is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl goes to Sweet's house and finds him with their close friends Ryder and Big Smoke.

main:29.text: The Green Sabre is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. The mission is a major turning point in the game. The three feuding families of the Grove Street Families have come together due to Carl's efforts and Sweet decides to finally get back at the Ballas.

main:30.text: Badlands is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by C.R.A.S.H. officers Frank Tenpenny, Eddie Pulaski and Jimmy Hernandez from a trailer in Angel Pine, Whetstone, San Andreas.

main:31.text: First Date is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his new girlfriend Michelle from her apartment in Rotterdam Hill, Broker, Liberty City. This mission introduces dating, and also gives the player an opportunity to play bowling. Niko will receive a call from Michelle (or to save time, Niko can call her) asking to go on a date.

main:32.text: Tanker Commander is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Catalina from the Gasso filling station in the town of Dillimore in Red County, San Andreas. As the gas station is confronted, Catalina points a shotgun at the two men in the store (through a window) and demands that they hand over the takings. The employee responds that the store has bullet-proof glass.

main:33.text: Body Harvest is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by pot-growing hippie The Truth from the U Get Inn Motel in the town of Angel Pine in Whetstone, San Andreas. Carl enters a motel room and finds Frank Tenpenny taking drugs. Tenpenny then introduces The Truth to Carl, and vice versa, saying that Carl will pay for the weed Tenpenny wants him to deliver.

main:34.text: King in Exile is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas veteran Cesar Vialpando from a home in the trailer park in the town of Angel Pine in Whetstone, San Andreas. Carl enters the trailer and finds Cesar and Kendl embracing each other. They greet Carl upon seeing him, and Cesar is furious over the recent events in Los Santos.

main:35.text: First Base is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Catalina from her hideout in Fern Ridge, Red County, San Andreas. It is unlocked by the mission King in Exile and any one of the four robbery missions given by Catalina. Catalina wanted Carl to return to her hideout to finish up robbing Red County.

main:36.text: Local Liquor Store is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Catalina from outside the Top Hat Liquor store in the town of Blueberry in Red County, San Andreas. Carl and Catalina arrive at P Hat Liquor in Blueberry, but some other robbers get there and rob the store themselves. The four robbers get on Quads, but Catalina manages to kill one as he is trying to escape.

main:37.text: Gone Courting is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Catalina from her hideout in Fern Ridge, Red County, San Andreas. It is unlocked by the mission First Base and any one of the four robbery missions given by Catalina. Catalina shows her love to Carl by tying him up and torturing him. This mission unlocks two out of a possible four robbery missions given by Catalina.

main:38.text: Against All Odds is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Catalina from outside the Inside Track betting shop in the town of Montgomery in Red County, San Andreas. Carl and Catalina arrive at the betting shop in Montgomery, having already decided to rob the shop at Catalina's hideout.

main:39.text: Made in Heaven is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Catalina from her hideout in Fern Ridge, Red County, San Andreas. It is unlocked by completing three of the four robbery missions given by Catalina. Catalina is in a bad mood and wants CJ to know that she doesn't love him anymore and wants to be just partners.

main:40.text: Small Town Bank is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Catalina from outside the bank in Palomino Creek, Red County, San Andreas. Carl and Catalina are planning on robbing the Palomino Creek Bank. They get into a vehicle and head off to their destination.

main:41.text: Wu Zi Mu is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando from an area just south of the town of Montgomery in Red County, San Andreas. Carl is waiting for Cesar in the meeting place, who is apparently late for a race. Later on, Cesar arrives, who explains that he is late because he did not know when the race would start.

main:42.text: Farewell, My Love... is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando from The Panopticon in Red County, San Andreas. Despite the mission being given by Cesar, he does not appear. It also features the final physical appearance of Catalina in the game. Catalina arrives at the meet. She kisses her new lover, as Carl notices her.

main:43.page: Are You Going to San Fierro?
main:43.text: Are You Going to San Fierro? is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by pot-growing hippie The Truth from his farm in Leafy Hollow, Flint County, San Andreas. After the completion of Farewell, My Love..., Catalina gives Carl a deed to an old Xoomer garage in Doherty, San Fierro. The Truth calls, stating that the weed is finally ready, and asks Carl to come see him.

main:44.text: Wear Flowers in Your Hair is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which protagonist Carl Johnson performs with the assistance of The Truth. It is started from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Carl, Cesar, Kendl and The Truth enter the garage in San Fierro. Carl is furious that Claude gave him a run-down, long-closed Xoomer gas station instead of a pink slip when he won the race.

main:45.text: 555 We Tip is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by C.R.A.S.H. officer Frank Tenpenny from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Despite being a C.R.A.S.H. mission, it is labelled as an independent mission from Carl, marked with a "CJ" icon. Tenpenny phones Carl, checking on him and how he's doing in San Fierro.

main:46.text: Deconstruction is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which protagonist Carl Johnson performs independently at the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Carl goes into the garage to check up on his new workforce, who are working on a Remington. Suddenly, an angry Kendl comes in and explains that construction workers from the construction site next to the garage have been harassing her.

main:47.text: Air Raid is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by electronics expert Zero from his store in Garcia, San Fierro, San Andreas. It is available after purchasing the store for $30,000. This mission is not mandatory to progress the storyline, but still necessary to achieve 100% game completion.

main:48.text: Supply Lines... is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by electronics expert Zero from his store in Garcia, San Fierro, San Andreas. CJ enters the shop, looking for Zero and ignoring his plea to leave him alone. CJ enters the back room of the shop, still looking for Zero, and finds him hanging by his underwear in a closet.

main:49.text: New Model Army is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by electronics expert Zero from his store in Garcia, San Fierro, San Andreas. Zero and Berkley have planned a showdown, the loser of which must leave San Fierro for good. The battle takes place inside the RC Battle Ground. To win, Zero must navigate across the area and safely get his RC Bandit into Berkley's compound.

main:51.text: Photo Opportunity is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. This mission is the introduction of a San Fierro Triads mission strand, although they are not introduced until the subsequent mission. Carl receives a phone call from Cesar Vialpando.

main:52.text: Jizzy is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu, also known as Woozie, from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. The subsequent part of the mission is given by the Loco Syndicate member Jizzy B. from his gentlemen's club Jizzy's Pleasure Domes in Battery Point.

main:53.text: T-Bone Mendez is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Loco Syndicate member Jizzy B. from his gentlemen's club Jizzy's Pleasure Domes in Battery Point, San Fierro, San Andreas. Jizzy argues with T-Bone Mendez (another person Carl has taken picture of earlier) about Jizzy's cut with the Loco Syndicate.

main:54.text: Mike Toreno is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Loco Syndicate member Jizzy B. from his gentlemen's club Jizzy's Pleasure Domes in Battery Point, San Fierro, San Andreas. T-Bone is convinced that the Loco Syndicate are being monitored. At that point, Mike Toreno calls T-Bone and explains that he is in danger and needs assistance.

main:55.text: Mountain Cloud Boys is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas. Carl arrives at Woozie's apartment and is led upstairs by a bodyguard, a Triad, who informs Carl that Woozie is actually blind and blessed with unbelievable good fortune.

main:56.text: Ran Fa Li is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas. Carl visits Woozie after helping him out in the last mission and is introduced to Ran Fa Li, the leader of the Red Gecko Tong.

main:57.text: Lure is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas. Ran Fa Li has gone to Woozie's apartment in Chinatown, but now the Da Nang Boys are after him and he can't get back home. The Triads are planning on how to lure the Da Nang Boys out of the way.

main:58.text: Amphibious Assault is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas. This mission can only be triggered between 20:00 and 6:00. Carl meets Wu Zi Mu at his apartment in Chinatown. Woozie explains that he plans to plant a bug on a Da Nang Boys-owned ship in San Fierro Bay.

main:59.text: The Da Nang Thang is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas. Carl bumps into Woozie just as he is about to leave his apartment.

main:60.text: Outrider is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Loco Syndicate member Jizzy B. from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. This mission is marked as part of the San Fierro Triads mission strand. Jizzy B. phones Carl and tells him, in a very suspiciously friendly tone, to get to a car in the Xoomer gas station at Easter Basin.

main:61.text: Snail Trail is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by C.R.A.S.H. officers Frank Tenpenny and Eddie Pulaski from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Carl enters the garage and is greeted by Jethro. He says that some cops are looking for him in the office. Carl realizes that it is Frank Tenpenny and Eddie Pulaski.

main:62.text: Ice Cold Killa is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Despite being a Triad-given mission, they do not make an appearance during the mission, but their involvement is still mentioned. This mission can only be triggered between 20:00 and 6:00.

main:63.text: Pier 69  is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triads from a rooftop across Pier 69 in Esplanade North, San Fierro, San Andreas. After finding out of the next meet between Big Smoke's lieutenant Ryder and the Loco Syndicate through killing Jizzy B., Carl calls Cesar to inform him of this.

main:64.text: Toreno's Last Flight is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Mike Toreno escaped death when Carl and Cesar Vialpando killed T-Bone Mendez and Ryder, but Wu Zi Mu has tracked Toreno down to a Maverick helicopter at the SFPD headquarters.

main:65.text: Yay Ka-Boom-Boom is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Cesar arrives at the garage and congratulates Carl for taking down the Loco Syndicate, but Carl is upset about the fact that he had to kill his childhood friend, Ryder.

main:66.text: Zeroing In is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Cesar, Carl, Dwaine, and Jethro are playing cards, until Kendl comes in and reprimands them. She tells them that they should be doing what they are supposed to do; make the garage a successful business.

main:67.text: Test Drive is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Cesar meets Carl at the Doherty Garage and informs him that he has located two more cars on the wishlist for the Wang Cars showroom. He suggests that he and Carl go to an automobile showroom across town.

main:68.text: Customs Fast Track is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Cesar is told that another car on their wish list, a Jester, is being loaded onto a container at a ship down at the docks at Easter Basin; his contact has marked the container.

main:69.text: Puncture Wounds is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas. Dwaine, Jethro, and Carl are all being idle, until Cesar comes in the garage in a Remington. Cesar is furious, having found yet another car on the wishlist but the vehicle is too fast and the driver is too quick.

main:70.text: Monster is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from his ranch near Robada Intersection in Tierra Robada, San Andreas. Carl is welcomed by a mysterious voice, who apparently knows a thing or two about his family. The voice says that Carl needs to impress him and let him see what Carl is made of.

main:71.text: Highjack is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from his ranch near Robada Intersection in Tierra Robada, San Andreas. Mike Toreno (who, as it turns out, was never in the helicopter Carl blew up) appears, and explains to Carl who he is and what he is here for.

main:72.text: Interdiction is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from his ranch near Robada Intersection in Tierra Robada, San Andreas. Toreno states that he needs a favor, but first, Carl asks about his brother. Toreno explains that he is in a prison upstate, and is all right.

main:73.text: Verdant Meadows is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from his ranch near Robada Intersection in Tierra Robada, San Andreas. Toreno tells Carl that he used Sweet as an excuse to get Carl to do jobs for him.

main:74.text: Learning to Fly is a mission strand in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from the Verdant Meadows Airfield in Bone County, San Andreas. After purchasing the Verdant Meadows Airfield, Toreno informs Carl via a phone call that he will be taking flying lessons.

main:75.text: N.O.E. is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from the Verdant Meadows Airfield in Bone County, San Andreas. Carl arrives at the airstrip, waiting for Toreno. Not long after, Toreno sneaks up behind Carl and grabs him in a chokehold.

main:76.text: Stowaway is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from the Verdant Meadows Airfield in Bone County, San Andreas. Carl is in the middle of the airstrip waiting for Toreno, when government agents arrive in trucks and a cargo plane. Feeling exposed, he hides behind some crates.

main:77.text: Black Project is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by pot-growing hippie The Truth from the Verdant Meadows Airfield in Bone County, San Andreas. Carl arrives at the airfield and is welcomed by The Truth, exercising on the top of an aircraft wreck. The Truth then berates Carl for having willfully worked for a government agent.

main:78.text: Green Goo is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by pot-growing hippie The Truth from the Verdant Meadows Airfield in Bone County, San Andreas. Carl is in the airstrip, sitting on a crate, looking and waiting for The Truth. Suddenly, The Truth comes out of nowhere, riding the Jetpack Carl retrieved from Area 69 back then, and nearly collides with Carl.

main:79.text: Fender Ketchup is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his office at The Four Dragons Casino, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Carl pays a visit to Woozie, after inviting him to this new place. Woozie explains to him the problems he's having about the casino business.

main:80.text: Explosive Situation is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his office at The Four Dragons Casino, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Carl has just frightened Johnny Sindacco into revealing that the Sindacco Crime Family has been responsible for the vandalism at Woozie's new casino venture.

main:81.text: You've Had Your Chips is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his office at The Four Dragons Casino, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Woozie and Carl are inside Woozie's office playing blackjack when Woozie's assistant comes in the office, presenting two casino chips to Woozie.

main:82.text: Don Peyote is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by The Truth via phone call from outside The Four Dragons Casino on The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Carl receives an unexpected phone call from The Truth. Apparently, he, a band and their manager went on a "peyote safari" in the desert a few nights earlier.

main:83.text: Architectural Espionage is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Wu Zi Mu as part of plans to pull off a heist of Caligula's Casino from the Four Dragons Casino in Las Venturas. Carl finds Woozie in a storage room in Woozie's casino. The two discuss the plans to rob Caligula's main vault, where the money is held.

main:84.text: Key to Her Heart is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Wu Zi Mu as part of plans to pull off a heist off Caligula's Palace from The Four Dragons Casino, located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Carl has just returned from the Las Venturas City Planning Department with the blueprints of Caligula's Palace, which he and Woozie intend to burglarize.

main:85.text: Dam and Blast is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Wu Zi Mu as part of plans to pull off a heist of Caligula's Palace from The Four Dragons Casino, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas.

main:86.text: Cop Wheels is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to the protagonist Carl Johnson by San Fierro Triads Leader Wu Zi Mu as part of plans to pull off a heist of Caligula's Casino from the Four Dragons Casino in Las Venturas.

main:87.text: Up, Up, and Away! is the second to last mission in the heist strand given to Carl Johnson by Wu Zi Mu in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. This mission can only be attempted between 20:00 and 6:00. Carl recently seized four HPV1000 Police motorcycles to be used as outriders to escort the armored van Carl plans to use to haul the off the cash.

main:88.text: Intensive Care is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by former lawyer and Leone Crime Family representative Ken Rosenberg from the Caligula's Palace, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Carl drops by the office and finds a problematic Rosenberg. Kent Paul persuades him to tell Carl his problems.

main:89.text: The Meat Business is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by former lawyer and Leone Crime Family representative Ken Rosenberg from the Caligula's Palace, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Ken Rosenberg has relapsed and is high on cocaine when Carl enters.

main:90.text: Fish in a Barrel is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his office at The Four Dragons Casino, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Although considered a mission by the game, it is merely a small cutscene.

main:91.text: Madd Dogg is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by rapper Madd Dogg from the Royal Casino, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Carl walks over to the south side of the casino, encountering two men encouraging someone on the casino roof to jump. One of them tells Carl that the person on the roof is Madd Dogg, a formerly successful rapper.

main:92.text: Freefall is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Leone Family Don Salvatore Leone from the Caligula's Palace, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Salvatore is sitting in his office at Caligula's Palace when Maria appears and gives him the sandwich he ordered.

main:93.text: Misappropriation is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by C.R.A.S.H. officer Frank Tenpenny from a house in Prickle Pine, Las Venturas, San Andreas. Carl visits C.R.A.S.H. at a house in Prickle Pine, Las Venturas and finds Tenpenny and Pulaski getting a grill ready and waiting for Hernandez to return with meat for the grill.

main:94.text: High Noon is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by C.R.A.S.H. officer Frank Tenpenny from Las Brujas ghost town in El Castillo del Diablo, Bone County, San Andreas. Carl is leaning against a post, waiting for Frank Tenpenny and his colleagues to arrive to retrieve the dossier Carl acquired. A Police Car approaches and C.R.A.S.H. emerges.

main:95.text: Saint Mark's Bistro is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Leone Family Don Salvatore Leone from the Caligula's Palace, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. It is the final mission from the Caligula's casino. Carl comes to visit Salvatore Leone at the office in Caligula's Palace to find him and Maria throwing knives at a tied-up Maccer.

main:96.text: Breaking the Bank at Caligula's is the final heist mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by San Fierro Triads leader Wu Zi Mu from The Four Dragons Casino, located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. Carl arrives at The Four Dragons Casino, dressed as a Caligula's employee, to meet Woozie and the crew in preparation for the heist.

main:98.text: Vertical Bird is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from Madd Dogg's Crib in Mulholland, Los Santos, San Andreas. After reclaiming Madd Dogg's mansion from the Vagos, Carl returns to the mansion, where he listens to Madd Dogg performing in his recording studio with Kent Paul and Maccer.

main:99.text: Home Coming is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from Madd Dogg's Crib in Mulholland, Los Santos, San Andreas. Inside the recording studio, Carl is on the phone discussing business, until Toreno snatches the phone and ends the call. He tells Carl he has one final job before he leaves Carl alone.

main:100.text: Cut Throat Business is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by rapper Madd Dogg from his mansion in Mulholland, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl arrives at the mansion to find Madd Dogg back in the studio and ready to make his comeback. On TV, rival rapper OG Loc is holding a press conference and music video shoot.

main:101.text: Beat Down on B Dup is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his mother's house in Grove Street, Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

main:102.text: Grove 4 Life is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Sweet is giving a group of Grove Street gang members a morale boosting talk when Carl enters. Sweet is glad to see him and wants to let the other gangs know that the Grove Street Families are back.

main:103.text: Riot  is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas that protagonist Carl Johnson performs independently at Madd Dogg's Crib in Mulholland, Los Santos, San Andreas. Frank Tenpenny, along with Eddie Pulaski, has finally been charged with racketeering, corruption, narcotics and sexual assault.

main:104.text: Los Desperados is the penultimate mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl drops by Sweet's house in Grove Street and starts to talk about the hood and the rioting going on.

main:105.text: End of the Line is the final storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. Carl and Sweet have managed to find out where their former friend, Big Smoke, is hiding. They drive over to Smoke's hideout in East Los Santos while avoiding rioters.

side:1.page: Vigilante in GTA Vice City Stories
side:1.text: Vigilante is a law enforcement vehicle-based side mission available in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories. In order to start the mission, the player must find a law enforcement vehicle and press the button shown on the instruction text (platform dependent) to toggle the side mission on or off. Once the mission is started, the player is given the criminal's last known location and a timer.

side:2.text: The City of Liberty Paramedics (COLP), also known simply as "MS Paramedics", are a medical service operating in Liberty City and the State of Alderney in Grand Theft Auto IV, Episodes from Liberty City and Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars. The MS Paramedics are the only medical service operating across Liberty City and Alderney in GTA IV and GTA Chinatown Wars. They operate a fleet of Ambulances.

side:4.text: Taxi Drivers are pedestrians appearing throughout the Grand Theft Auto series. They are employed to drive taxicabs around the game world, picking up and dropping off fares. The player may perform the very same activity in multiple titles of the series. Over the years of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, the taxi and cabbie drivers have evolved considerably.

side:5.text: Burglar is a vehicle side-mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The mission is started by entering a unique variant of the Boxville (called BoxBurg) and manually starting the mission using the vehicle side-mission button. The Burglar mission can only be triggered between 20:00 and 06:00, otherwise the player is instructed to return to the vehicle at that specific time to start the mission.

side:6.text: Pimping is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas that consists of driving prostitutes to meet their clients. The mission can be triggered in any of the main cities in San Andreas while driving a Broadway, but not when in the countryside.

side:7.text: The Freight Train Challenge is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The mission involves the player transporting freight around the state in a Brown Streak or a Freight under a time limit. The challenge is available after completing Yay Ka-Boom-Boom. Like most side missions, it is activated by pressing the sub-mission button.

side:8.text: The BMX Challenge is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The mission is started by entering a parked BMX in Glen Park Skate Park with a cycling skill of 20% or more. The goal of the mission is to collect 19 floating coronas around the skate park before the countdown timer runs out of time. The timer starts when the cutscene finishes. Each corona will add 10 seconds to the timer.

side:9.text: The NRG-500 Challenge is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The mission is started by entering a parked NRG-500 at a dry dock in Easter Basin, San Fierro. The goal is to collect 18 floating coronas around the dry dock before the countdown timer runs out of time. The countdown timer starts at 10 seconds when the cutscene ends. Each corona will add 10 seconds to the timer.

side:10.text: The Chiliad Challenge is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The mission is started by entering a parked Mountain Bike on top of Mount Chiliad between 7:00 and 18:00 and having a cycling skill above 40%. The goal of the mission is to be the first to reach the base of the mountain while racing with other mountain bikers down the mountain.

side:11.text: Courier is a side-mission strand in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The mission is a package delivery side-mission, serving as a spiritual successor to the Pizza Boy Mission in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. The side-mission strand offers assets which generate money periodically for the player to collect at each location where the mission is available – one business in each of the three cities.

side:12.text: The Valet mission is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. These mission is triggered when Carl Johnson walks into the red marker in front of the Vank Hoff Hotel in Financial, San Fierro, just north of the Big Pointy Building, but only when wearing the Valet Uniform. The mission, along with the required outfit, becomes available only after completion of the mission 555 We Tip.

side:13.text: Trucking is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The missions become available after completing Catalina's mission, Tanker Commander, which features Mr. Whittaker, an employee at the RS Haul Depot in Flint County, just west of Los Santos and north of Helena Wankstein's Farm. After that, there should be a red marker within the depot compound. To start a trucking mission, simply walk into the marker.

side:14.text: Quarry Survival is a Survival job in Grand Theft Auto Online as part of the continuation of The Cayo Perico Heist update, released on July 8, 2021, during the Survivals Week event. It takes place at Davis Quartz in the San Chianski Mountain Range. The enemies at the start of the first wave are quarry workers with melee weapons or pistols. From wave 2 onwards, the enemies are Merryweather Security mercenaries.

side:15.text: The Bike School is an activity in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It consists of six lessons in the form of selectable courses, each completed by achieving at least a bronze medal in the final results. All six lessons are required for 100% completion and can be done during or after the story completion. Mission failure will occur if the player gets wasted, stops or destroys the vehicle during a test.

side:16.text: The Boat School is an activity in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It consists of five lessons in the form of selectable courses, each completed by achieving at least a bronze medal in the final results. All five lessons are required for 100% completion and can be done during or after the story completion. Mission failure will occur if the player gets wasted, stops or destroys the vehicle during a test.

side:17.text: The Pilot School is an activity in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It consists of ten lessons in the form of selectable courses, each completed by achieving at least a bronze medal in the final results. All ten lessons are required for the story progression. Mission failure will occur if the player is wasted or ditches the plane during the mission (indirectly destroying it).

collectible:1.text: Tags are a collectible in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. There are 100 Tags located all around Los Santos, which the player must find and paint a Grove Street Families tag over it using a Spray Can while on foot. A tag needs at least 29 units of Spray Can "ammo" to be completely sprayed over.

collectible:2.text: Snapshots are a collectible in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. There are 50 Snapshots located all around San Fierro and city limits, which the player must find and photograph using a Camera. The Camera has several spawn points in San Fierro, all located near Snapshot locations.

collectible:3.text: Horseshoes are a collectible in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. There are 50 Horseshoes located all around Las Venturas, which the player must find and collect while on foot. Each Horseshoe collected rewards the player with $100 and 20 points of "Luck" in the Stats menu (which does not affect the gameplay in any way), totaling $5,000 and 1000 "Luck" points for collecting all Horseshoes.

collectible:4.text: Oysters are a collectible in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. There are 50 Oysters located all around San Andreas, which the player must find and collect while swimming. Each Oyster collected rewards the player with $100, totaling $5,000 for collecting all Oysters alone. Collecting all 50 Oysters is a requirement for the 100% completion.

collectible:5.text: Unique Stunt Jumps (also known as Unique Jumps in 3D Universe and Stunt Jumps in GTA IV) are a feature in every Grand Theft Auto game since GTA III (with the exception of GTA Advance). All GTA games have jumps set up around their maps for "insane" stunting.

main:50.text: The Driving School is an activity in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The Driving School consists of 12 lessons in the form of selectable courses, each completed by achieving at least a bronze medal in the final results. All these lessons are required to expand the Doherty Garage operation to the nearby Wang Cars. It is not required for main storyline progression and can be done after the story completion.

easter-egg:1.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:1.text: Inside one of the guard booths (the one that is near the spawn location of Leviathan and Raindance) within the Easter Bay Airport, there is a computer running 3ds Max (Autodesk tool used by Rockstar North to create the models for the RenderWare-based titles), showing a screenshot of the interior props found in the Las Venturas City Planning Department.

easter-egg:2.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:2.text: Near Catalina's cabin, there are three graves and a shovel, suggesting she may have murdered and buried past lovers prior to meeting Carl Johnson.

easter-egg:3.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:3.text: At the visitor center below Katie Zhan's House, there is a list of facts about the Gant Bridge, one of which reads "Takes up a staggering 1.27mb of disk space." In, the sign is updated to reflect the size of the new version of the bridge, reading that it "Takes up a staggering 38.9mb of disk space."

easter-egg:4.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:4.text: On top of the Gant Bridge, there is a sign that reads "There are no easter eggs up here. Go away."

easter-egg:5.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:5.text: Near Area 69, there is a hole that is filled with six body bags.

easter-egg:6.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:6.text: In the Palomino Creek graveyard, there is a grave which reads "R.I.P Scott Wilson", referring to the Rockstar North level designer who worked on the countryside areas of the game.

easter-egg:7.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:7.text: On the top floor of the Las Venturas City Planning Department, a model of Caligula's Palace can be found with a Rockstar logo on it.

easter-egg:8.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:8.text: Some of the clothing that the player wears, as well the suitcase at the start of the game that CJ holds while in the airport, and more items have the Rockstar Games logo on them.

easter-egg:9.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:9.text: The parachute has a small Rockstar North logo on the back.

easter-egg:10.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:10.text: If viewing the San Fierro Tower at night from the south, the player can see the Rockstar Games logo being shown as the lighting of the building.

easter-egg:11.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:11.text: At night, if the player looks up in the sky, there are stars that form the letter R in reference to the Rockstar Games logo, with a larger star representing the star from the logo.

easter-egg:12.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:12.text: The kites and sailboats inside Zero RC have the Rockstar logo on them.

easter-egg:13.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:13.text: Carcer Gas cylinders are from Carcer City, the setting of Manhunt.

easter-egg:14.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:14.text: Inside Big Smoke's Crack Palace, there is a doormat that reads "Not Welcome Rockstar North" with the Rockstar North logo in the center.

easter-egg:15.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:15.text: Part of the text on the side of the Hydra features the letters "DMA"; this is likely a reference to Rockstar North since the company was formerly known as DMA Design. DMA is also a play on United States Marine Corps squadrons that use the McDonnell Douglas AV-8B Harrier II (VMA).

easter-egg:16.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:16.text: On the top floor of the Las Venturas City Planning Department, the blueprints of from Manhunt can be seen on the wall.

easter-egg:17.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:17.text: Inside Las Venturas Police Headquarters, there are pictures of James Earl Cash and members of from Rockstar North's Manhunt.

easter-egg:18.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:18.text: Northstar Rock is a reference to Rockstar North.

easter-egg:19.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:19.text: The cheat code "Chaos Mode" could reference Rockstar and VIS Entertainment's 2001 game, State of Emergency (video game). Chaos Mode was one of the playable game modes in this game.

easter-egg:20.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:20.text: The Gasso gas station in Dillimore has a sign on its window reading "Max Pane- Bulletproof Glass". This is a reference to Remedy Entertainment's Max Payne franchise, published by Rockstar Games.

easter-egg:21.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:21.text: Carl's wardrobe contains a surfboard with an image of Vice City on it.

easter-egg:22.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:22.text: In Denise Robinson's house, there is a poster of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City's box art on her bedroom wall.

easter-egg:23.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:23.text: In the mission Black Project, the player can spot a crowbar on a table in a lab. This is a reference to Valve's 1998 game Half-Life (video game).

easter-egg:24.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:24.text: In the mission Black Project, after the player enters the base and the alarm is raised, one of the voice announcements says "Personnel reminded that running in corridors whilst holding scissors is not permitted". This is a possible reference to the video game company Running with Scissors, best known for its Postal (video game) games, which are considered by some to be "GTA Clones".

easter-egg:25.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:25.text: The Zombotech Corporation is most likely a reference to the Umbrella Corporation from the Resident Evil (series) series. Also, based on a diagram on the wall, there appears to be a large underground facility reminiscent of from the Resident Evil film.

easter-egg:26.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:26.text: The Trip Skip icon features the side profile of the Deluxo, a car mostly inspired by the DeLorean DMC-12 that is otherwise absent from the game. This is a reference to the Back to the Future franchise, which features a DeLorean-based time machine.

easter-egg:27.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:27.text: The finance company named J. Bond Bail Bonds is a reference to James Bond.

easter-egg:28.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:28.text: The scene in the mission Just Business featuring a Packer jumping off a surface road in slow motion into a storm drain channel, which Big Smoke and CJ are using to escape, is a nod to a similar scene in the 1991 film Terminator 2: Judgment Day, where a large tow-truck executes a similar stunt as it is in pursuit of John Connor.

easter-egg:29.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:29.text: When Cesar asks CJ if he'd like to make some money, CJ responds "Does the pope shit in the woods?", a malapropism coined by The Dude in The Big Lebowski.

easter-egg:30.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA San Andreas
easter-egg:30.text: The Cobra Marital Arts gym is probably a reference to the Cobra Martial Arts gym in the movie The Karate Kid.
